title: Baking soda and cream of tartar for baking powder

evidence.basis: B8, an ENGINEERING SELECTION, not consensus and not culinary validation. OD-7 (owner commission 2026-10-08, ENGINEERING only; not culinary validation, not released guidance). Evidence: private/research/substitution-knowledge (2026-10-07). Selected: America's Test Kitchen 1/4 tsp soda + 1/2 tsp cream of tartar per 1 tsp baking powder, 'Use right away' (SRC-LV-01#a; also SRC-LV-02#d 'Use immediately'); the same ratio from KA SRC-LV-06#j, Land O'Lakes SRC-LV-13#a, Arm & Hammer SRC-LV-09#f. Competing, kept: 1/4 tsp soda + 5/8 tsp cream of tartar (NDSU SRC-LV-15#b, USU SRC-LV-17#b, CSU SRC-LV-16#a); NDSU also 1/3 tsp soda + 1/2 tsp. Enforced: oven-heating step before the dry mix, a dough-mixing and a baking step after it, no rest, chill or hold from the dry mix through baking (an unrecognized step leaves it unknown), volume amounts only (no sourced weights). Input bounds 1/2 tsp-2 tbsp are engineering bounds.

ops.text: Have the oven hot before the liquid goes in: once the dough is wet, the baking soda and cream of tartar start working, so shape it and bake it straight away, without resting or chilling it.

consequence.headline: Use baking soda with cream of tartar instead of the baking powder, and bake as soon as the dough is mixed.
consequence.reason: Baking powder is baking soda with a powdered acid; cream of tartar supplies the acid. This uses America's Test Kitchen's proportions; some extension guides use a little more cream of tartar.
consequence.tradeoff: The mix starts working as soon as it's wet and keeps nothing back for the oven, so the dough can't wait. Not kitchen-tested in this recipe.

proposal.text: Yes, with cream of tartar alongside the baking soda.
